options.rationale: MFCC extraction starts by splitting audio into overlapping 20 to 30 millisecond frames. Good framing helps create meaningful feature vectors for later modeling.

options.text: The Mel scale should match human hearing sensitivity
options.rationale: The Mel scale adjusts frequency bins to match how people perceive pitch. It emphasizes ranges important to speech and compresses less important ranges.

options.text: Every raw audio sample must be stored as the final feature
options.error_type: confuses compact feature vectors with raw sample storage
options.rationale: MFCCs summarize each frame instead of storing every sample. The goal is a compact feature vector that captures spectral shape.
options.better_fit: This fits the earlier raw audio stage before pre-processing compresses the signal into features.

feedback.intrinsic: The meeting recorder may keep too much raw detail and still provide poor features for recognition.
feedback.instructional: MFCCs are useful because they compress audio while preserving speech characteristics. Final features are summaries, not every raw sample.

options.text: The decoder should create the MFCC coefficients
options.error_type: confuses feature extraction with decoding
options.rationale: MFCC coefficients are created during pre-processing. Decoding happens later, when possible word sequences are searched and scored.
options.better_fit: This fits when acoustic and language predictions already exist and the best text hypothesis must be selected.

feedback.intrinsic: The review may focus on a later transcript-selection step while the feature vectors remain poorly formed.
feedback.instructional: MFCC settings belong before acoustic modeling. Decoding cannot create the coefficients needed by earlier stages.

payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. MFCC extraction checks include short overlapping frames and Mel-scale mapping that reflects human hearing.

payload.prompt: A product owner for voice-driven customer service says, 'Our recognizer is weak, so the acoustic model must be the only issue.' Which other pipeline causes should you also consider?

options.rationale: Poor capture can come from background noise, microphone quality, or distance from the speaker. Because each stage builds on the previous one, bad input can hurt all later stages.
A weak language model can struggle with vocabulary, grammar, common word patterns, or domain terms. That can cause transcription errors even when acoustic modeling is not the only issue.
Post-processing applies formatting and corrections to final text. If those rules are too aggressive, they can damage the transcript after decoding.

options.error_type: confuses recognition quality with synthesis voice output
options.rationale: Text-to-speech voice style affects generated spoken audio. It does not explain weak transcription in speech recognition.
options.better_fit: This fits when evaluating speech synthesis output, such as tone, pace, or speaking style.

feedback.intrinsic: The customer service team may spend effort on voice output while caller transcripts remain inaccurate.
feedback.instructional: Recognition quality should be traced through capture, modeling, decoding, and cleanup. Voice style belongs to speech synthesis.

payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. Recognition quality can fail at capture, language modeling, or post-processing, not only acoustic modeling.

flashcards.back: A microphone converts sound waves into a digital signal.
Compact audio features that emphasize speech-relevant frequencies.
Phoneme probability predictions from audio feature vectors.
Use vocabulary, grammar, and patterns to predict word sequences.
